title: Valid Anagram
prompt: Given two strings `s` and `t`, return `true` if `t` is an anagram of `s`, and `false` otherwise. An anagram uses exactly the same letters with exactly the same frequency, just rearranged.

examples.explanation: Single-character strings, the minimum length allowed, are trivially anagrams of themselves when equal.

constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters
hints: If the lengths differ, they can't be anagrams — check that first as a cheap early exit.
Counting each character's frequency in both strings and comparing the counts works without sorting.
A single array of 26 counters (or a hash map) can be incremented for `s` and decremented for `t` in one pass; if everything nets to zero, it's an anagram.

solution.approach: Compare lengths first as a fast rejection. Then use one frequency map: increment counts for each character in `s`, decrement for each character in `t`. If any count is non-zero at the end, the strings aren't anagrams.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(1) — at most 26 distinct lowercase letters
